neighbours.label: A small number word that opens a rate, duration or range ('every three to seven years', 'three to four times a week', 'within two decades'), vs a number that counts objects
fire: Doctors suggest checking your blood pressure every two to three months.
The comet passes close to Earth roughly once every seventy years, and its tail lasts for two weeks.
Water the seedlings two or three times a day during hot weather.
Most patients recover within three weeks of the operation.
The festival is held every four years in a different city.
Volcanoes in the region erupt every five to ten centuries.
Take one tablet two times a day after meals.
The bridge should be finished within two years, the mayor said.
quiet: Doctors in the clinic saw two patients before lunch on Monday.
The comet was photographed by three astronomers from the hill.
We planted two rows of seedlings beside the garden fence.
Most of the three patients went home after the operation.
The festival hired four bands and a choir from the city.
The museum owns five paintings by the same artist.
She bought two tablets and a phone at the store.
The mayor said two bridges will be repainted.

predictions: Number words opening a frequency, duration or range reach 0.3-0.9; number words counting people or things stay under 0.06.
short: number opening a rate or time span
notes: Card: top examples peak on ' three' x10, ' two' x7, ' one' x3, mostly in 'every N to M' and 'N or M times'. Probe: 'every three to seven years' 0.925, 'within two decades' 0.640, 'three to four times a week' 0.580, 'every one to two hours' 0.437, '20%' 0.323; 'Three students won prizes' 0.011, 'He has two brothers' 0.045.
